sources.claim: On September 26, 1983, the Soviet Oko early-warning system reported five missiles launched from the United States.
Petrov was the duty officer who judged the report to be a false alarm.
The alert was later attributed to sunlight reflecting from cloud tops and being misread by the satellite system.
The event's historical significance must be framed cautiously; available analysis does not establish that a retaliatory launch was definitely imminent.
